proposal.name: Check unchanged Python applications against their models

issue_plan.name: Check unchanged Python applications against their models
issue_plan.summary: Complete issue #313 in three reviewable changes: execute application checks with evidence bound to real implementation calls, connect sampled conformance and runtime results to the gate and receipts, then add exhaustive, attempted-step and applicable larger-bound checks. Reuse the application staging and dependency foundation, preserve original source bytes and existing language behavior, and grant only the evidence the runs establish. Each change keeps SPEC.md and README accurate; the completed path includes a usable manual adoption example and real Python, TLC and Docker integration coverage. The merger must record the existing-code execution policy extension and run unavailable Docker or network checks on the final head; factory drafting and synthesis remain deferred.

issues.title: Execute Python application checks with bound implementation observations
issues.body:
Build the execution adapter needed by #313, the second step of #294's ratified adoption plan. The base already admits Python existing manifests through project.ResolvePythonApplication and copies full applications through verify.StagePythonApplication; PythonApplicationWorkspace.SelectImage admits root requirements and returns dependency evidence. Component discovery and result-attribution APIs exist, but verify.Check, verify.Run and the direct Python runner still refuse this mode. This issue adds a directly testable execution adapter and its evidence contract; public gate admission remains refused until the following issue connects TLC and report attribution.

Execute configured application tests and conformance drivers in the staged application layout, with application-relative component references, inputs and invocation working directories and verification-project-relative manifest paths. Support the ordinary Python invocation forms used by the foundation: python -m unittest with selected test names or modules, and python followed by the configured driver script and ordered arguments. Validate supported invocation forms before tools or dependency installation; reject unsupported commands, proof invocations and requests whose meaning cannot be preserved. Do not execute declaration strings through a shell or silently substitute another command. Record declared invocation identity separately from the actual absolute interpreter, launcher, arguments, working directory, explicit environment and effective sampling. Protect gate-owned environment and startup settings from declaration overrides. Preserve inert discovery and caller-supplied attribution APIs.

Use StagePythonApplication and SelectImage, including the standard-library path without requirements, recursive root requirements and constraints, original/canonical hashes and wheel evidence. Prepare one immutable dependency image for a verification session, pass it to executions, and expose enough session state for later ordinary and larger-bound runs to reuse it without resolving dependencies again. Keep #227's pinned absolute interpreter, controlled startup without site/user-site processing or implicit source paths, PYTHONHASHSEED=0, trusted runtime and standard library precedence, application root and driver directory before installed libraries, including namespace packages. Execute offline with the existing Docker isolation, proxy suppression, resource limits and cancellation cleanup. Installation network belongs only to the existing dependency-image builder; failures never fall back to another environment. No application source annotation or # +nagini marker is required, and this adapter never invokes Nagini.

Provide gate-owned observation collection that associates each conformance observation with the actual selected staged source and lexical symbol, executed call, driver and invocation. The driver must exercise surrounding application behavior which calls the modeled component, and read back state from that implementation. Verify the correspondence between implementation calls and the recorded pre/post states, rather than accepting a driver-authored lifecycle plus a separate list of imported or called symbols. Reject an unused selected target, a replaced callable, another symbol from the same file, a driver that merely imports the target, and a driver that calls or touches the real target while reporting a substitute object's lifecycle. Binding must remain valid across runs and instances; evidence from one invocation must not satisfy another. Establish the initial-state read-back as well as transitions. Missing, empty, malformed, stale or inconsistent execution evidence and import/runtime failures must produce a failed execution with useful diagnostics, never successful conformance evidence. Define and document the driver observation interface in this change so subsequent issues use it without changing application source.

Collect actual test execution and per-test outcomes, including failures, errors and skips, from the runner. A selected test declaration or a passing package/process is insufficient: identify which configured tests really executed and whether they completed successfully. An unexecuted, skipped or failed required configured test must be distinguishable from a passing test and must not qualify for later gate success. Do not infer target coverage from a passing test, and do not fabricate assertion records when the runner did not observe assertions.

Hash actual staged application inputs, including unselected siblings, resources, tests, driver, manifest, lock, model and includes, together with dependency and trusted-runner evidence. Preserve the full staged input snapshot without expanding production scope. Bind observations and outcomes to that snapshot and detect changes that would make the execution's source identity stale. Keep evidence deterministic and independent of host paths or temporary run identifiers. Return raw execution outcomes and observations for later TLC checking, not a proof or a model-conformance verdict. Initially provide sampled executions; do not claim exhaustive or attempted-step coverage from a declaration or harness import.

Tests must run real Python in Docker against an unchanged task-lifecycle package with a sibling import, a resource read and an installed third-party wheel. Its driver must call an application entry point which calls the selected lifecycle component. Assert captured real calls and state read-backs, executed test names/outcomes, deterministic repeated runs, and byte-for-byte unchanged original application files after success and failure. Include unused/import-only targets, replaced callables, a touched real target with a substitute lifecycle, mismatched invocation evidence, malformed/missing output, failed or unexecuted configured tests, and import/runtime errors. Test controlled startup, effective hash seed, namespace import precedence, offline execution and immutable image selection with and without dependencies; doubles may test orchestration but cannot replace the real execution tests. Preserve legacy Python, marked-file and TypeScript execution. Keep the public existing-Python rejection tests here, since the gate is not yet connected.

Update SPEC.md and README in this PR to describe the adapter and observation interface as available while public gate execution is still unavailable. Cite the recorded decisions on changed SPEC bullets and the ratified #313 child plan for the extension. Foundations: D-0013 (recorded tool evidence), D-0029 and D-0047 (deterministic conformance), D-0054 (existing code), D-0158, D-0168 and D-0177 (component identities, inert invocation provenance and Python discovery), D-0170 and D-0171 (independent conformance/runtime results), D-0178 (#227 dependency and startup policy), and D-0122 (current documentation); reuse #310's application-context contract. A plumbing build cannot edit decisions/; the merger records the new execution/observation policy and its dependencies with decision tooling. Real Docker/network checks unavailable to the factory belong under Merger work, with a documented command and passing output on the final PR head. Factory drafting, synthesis and proof adapters are out of scope.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Gate sampled Python application conformance and report actual results
issues.body:
Connect #313's Python application execution adapter, merged by the preceding issue, to the normal verification gate. The repository now has full-application staging, dependency-image selection and a tested runner that binds real implementation calls and state observations to source, symbol, driver and invocation. Use those capabilities to make manual adoption of unchanged Python applications work through verify.Check, verify.Run, language routing, direct Python checks and CLI toolchain preparation. This issue completes sampled model testing and runtime evidence; the next issue connects bounded-exhaustive, attempted-step and applicable larger-bound checks.

Replace the blanket ErrComponents/ErrPythonApplication refusals with one consistent capability check. Admit Python existing applications using the supported test/driver invocation forms and observation contract, with explicit components when configured. Preserve legacy inventory mode when components are omitted rather than inferring component scope; such runs must still establish execution provenance for selected existing source and use the manifest driver. Reject unsupported component languages/modes, proof selections, unsupported invocation forms, inconsistent selections and unsupported evidence modes before verification tools or dependency installation. A malformed explicit configuration must not fall through to a legacy runner. Until the following issue connects their checks, reject existing-Python exhaustive and attempted-step requests explicitly instead of silently downgrading them to sampled success. Preserve model-only checking and the old Python and TypeScript paths. Update obsolete existing-Python rejection assertions, retaining rejection coverage for genuinely unsupported configurations.

Stage and resolve all application, driver and model inputs for a session before executing them; use only those snapshots for code execution, TLC, attribution and hashing. Select the staged application's admitted dependency image once and retain its immutable identity and resolution evidence for every execution in the session. Route this conformance-only mode to no proof tool: no Nagini annotation or marker is required, ordinary modules never reach Nagini, and even a marker cannot silently enable proof in this mode. Keep the preceding runner's offline environment, startup/import policy, fixed hash seed and cleanup.

Use existing TLC trace checking at the ratified bounds to check actual implementation observations against Init and Next, preserving batched checking and deterministic runs. Continue all existing applicable model, statement-pin, ratification, witness, fairness and known-bug gate checks. Gate success requires successful required configured tests, usable bound execution evidence, and successful conformance as well as the existing design checks. Import/runtime failures, missing or malformed evidence, an unused or substituted target, an invalid transition and failed/skipped/unexecuted required configured tests all fail the gate. Diagnostics must identify the failed check or missing evidence. A successful process or a plausible trace without implementation binding cannot pass.

Populate Report components through the existing conformance and runtime attribution APIs from execution and TLC results, with exact target/check IDs and actual invocation, runner/tool pins, inputs, model/includes, ratified bounds, effective sampling, observations, counts, outcomes and diagnostics. Never turn intended invocations into successful result rows or infer execution of one check from another. Keep configured assumptions assumed/unverified, all components without their own successful conformance evidence unchecked for conformance, and every component without proof unchecked for proof. Runtime rows report tests actually exercised and their independent outcomes; they grant no target coverage, and assertions appear only with actual evidence. Preserve valid independent observations when another check fails while the overall gate fails. Maintain the supplied APIs' transactional validation and independent evidence semantics.

JSON, Markdown and fingerprints must describe what ran and what TLC checked. Include actual application files/resources, dependency resolution, runner/driver bytes, model/includes, bounds and sampling; changed inputs or observations must change the fingerprint even if all counts and pass/fail outcomes remain the same. Identical repeated executions and relocated identical applications must retain deterministic evidence fingerprints, excluding timestamps, host paths and ephemeral IDs. Explicit reports must distinguish gate-produced execution from externally supplied results without weakening validation or making a supplied row itself a gate verdict. Render all untrusted evidence safely under the existing receipt rules. Grant only tested-against-the-model evidence for sampled observations, no exhaustive-state/every-step label, no proof and no project-wide every-size claim. Keep uncovered components visible and legacy receipts unchanged.

Add end-to-end acceptance and real Docker integration tests using real Python and TLC for an unchanged task-lifecycle application with sibling code, resource access and an installed third-party wheel. The valid lifecycle passes verify.Run and produces accurate JSON and Markdown; a real invalid transition fails. Drivers that never call the selected implementation, only import it, or touch/call it while reporting a substitute lifecycle must fail. Include runtime/import errors, a failing selected test alongside passing tests, a selected test not actually run, malformed/missing evidence and unsupported preflight without tool calls. Check deterministic repeated runs, relocation, changed source/sibling/resource/test/driver/model/include/requirements/bounds/sampling inputs and unchanged original source bytes. Test explicit inventory with unchecked neighboring components and the no-components path without invented component inventory. Demonstrate that no Nagini tool is prepared or called; run regressions for existing Python, marked-file Python and TypeScript. Orchestration doubles are supplemental, not substitutes for the real gate tests.

Update SPEC.md and README in the same PR, replacing claims that all existing-Python/component execution is unavailable with the exact supported sampled capability and current coverage limits. Supply a usable manual adoption example: application and verification directory layout, existing and component selections, unittest and driver invocations, dependencies/resource, model and genuinely ratified bounds, observation/read-back driver usage, the verify command and expected receipt/failure behavior. Do not fabricate a ratification or edit existing locks. Document that the factory does not yet draft or synthesize this path and that exhaustive/attempt coverage is still rejected pending the next issue.

This implements #313 on #310's application-context foundation and the preceding execution adapter. Decisions: D-0013, D-0024, D-0029, D-0047 and D-0054 ground testing and existing-code conformance; D-0158, D-0168, D-0177 and D-0178 ground identities, invocations, Python discovery and dependencies; D-0161, D-0163, D-0169, D-0170, D-0171 and D-0175 ground independent evidence and receipts; D-0122 requires current docs with decision citations on changed SPEC bullets. The ratified child plan supplies the new gate execution policy until the merger records it with decision tooling, since plumbing cannot write decisions/. Unavailable Docker/network validation is Merger work: document the integration command and require passing real Python/TLC/Docker output at the final PR head before moving on. Do not implement proof adapters, factory drafting or synthesis.

issues.title: Check exhaustive Python applications and applicable larger bounds
issues.body:
Finish #313 after the sampled existing-Python gate and execution-evidence adapter have merged. The preceding changes run unchanged applications offline, bind real source/symbol calls and read-back states to the driver and invocation, check sampled traces with TLC, execute configured tests and populate runtime/conformance receipts. Extend that same path to claimed bounded-exhaustive coverage, attempted-step checks and applicable one-size-larger checks. This completes the whole existing-code execution stage of #294; no required #313 work is left for a later adoption stage.

Admit supported exhaustive and attempted-step configurations through the shared capability check, public gate and direct execution path. Reuse the existing conformance.Check, attempted-step and trusted exploration-harness semantics rather than introducing a second model checker. Explore actual application behavior at the ratified bounds and feed implementation-bound observations into TLC. Preserve the separation between checked observed transitions, exhaustive state coverage and tried steps: sampled results never earn exhaustive claims, bounded-exhaustive claims require positive matching implementation/model state counts and successful conformance, and every-step claims require actual nonempty successful attempt checking. Failed attempted-step checks fail the gate and block exhaustive/every-step labels while preserving successful observed-transition evidence. An absent attempt record must not become a successful every-step check. Do not manufacture stronger evidence from an exhaustive flag, harness import, matching counts alone or driver-owned substitute state. Maintain the established qualification rules for exhausted states with absent attempts and the existing environment-bound exceptions in attempted-step checking.

When existing rules make the larger-bound check applicable, run TLC and the application exploration at the actual increased bounds using the same immutable admitted dependency image and staged application snapshot as the ordinary run. Keep the existing model/driver bound mapping, numeric and numbered-model-value growth, parameter/environment distinctions and count/depth comparison. Adapt the application path and bound plumbing so sibling imports, resources, third-party libraries and component attribution still work when the verification directory is nested. Only driver/environment copies may be changed to supply increased bounds; selected application implementation bytes must remain unchanged. Record the effective driver/environment inputs and hashes and actual bounds for this run separately from the ratified ordinary ones, without rewriting the original driver, ratified lock or statements or falsely attributing larger bounds to the ordinary component result.

A successful required larger-bound comparison needs real implementation execution and valid bound observations/counts, not a driver-created count file or imported target. Retain provenance enforcement in counting mode, including rejection of an unused, replaced or merely touched target with a substitute lifecycle. Runtime/import errors and missing/malformed execution evidence fail the relevant required check. Preserve existing larger-check qualifications: if larger TLC cannot finish within its established allowance or finds a model problem, claim no larger success and do not fail solely for that optional model-side result; when TLC establishes the comparison and the implementation disagrees or fails, fail as required by the existing gate policy. Preserve the existing distinct unfinished implementation-exploration outcome instead of turning a timeout into success. Report applicability, actual attempts, errors, timeouts and qualifications faithfully.

Extend component conformance attribution, JSON, Markdown and fingerprints to retain actual ordinary and larger bounds, mode, sampling, tool pins, all input/driver/dependency evidence, implementation observations and check outcomes. Do not mix larger observations with ratified-bound rows or let stale qualification flags survive a changed input. A passing larger check grants no proof or project-wide every-size claim. Uncovered components remain unchecked; tests do not become target coverage. Preserve independent runtime/test outcomes, assumptions and supplied-evidence API behavior, and the established legacy Python, marked-file Python and TypeScript paths and receipts.

Extend the real task-lifecycle fixture and real Python/TLC/Docker integration suite from the preceding issues. A complete bounded exploration passes; a sampled run visiting the same finite states still has no exhaustive label; a driver missing a reachable state fails its exhaustive claim; successful attempts and missing/refused/omitted steps demonstrate the distinct qualifications and fail gates where required. Exercise applicable larger success, a real implementation mismatch at larger bounds, nonapplicability and existing model-timeout/model-failure qualifications. Include larger-run unused/import-only/touched-substitute targets and malformed count/evidence failures. Verify one immutable dependency image across ordinary and larger executions even if a mutable cache tag changes, fixed hash seed and offline startup/import precedence in both runs, deterministic reruns and fingerprints, changed model/includes/bounds/driver/resources/dependency inputs, and byte-for-byte unchanged application source and original driver after every success/failure case. Keep the valid, invalid-transition, unused-target, substitute-lifecycle, test-failure and runtime/import-failure sampled acceptance cases running as regressions. Ensure the final integration entry point exercises the complete #313 matrix with real Python, TLC and the installed wheel; do not replace it with Docker doubles.

Update SPEC.md and README in this PR to remove the intermediate sampled-only limitation and make the manual adoption example usable for sampled and exhaustive/attempt modes and applicable larger bounds. State what evidence each mode earns, actual bounds and dependencies, how real surrounding application calls and read-backs are supplied, how configured test outcomes are recorded, and why uncovered components, proof and every-size claims remain out of scope. Reconcile all now-obsolete 'component execution unavailable' statements, without implying support for unsupported languages/configurations or ordinary proof adapters. Factory drafting and synthesis remain deferred.

Foundations are D-0013, D-0024, D-0029, D-0047 and D-0054 for actual testing, D-0068, D-0070 and D-0076 for larger bounds, D-0082, D-0085 and D-0088 for exploration and attempted steps, D-0158, D-0168, D-0177 and D-0178 for provenance and Python environment policy, and D-0161, D-0163, D-0169, D-0170, D-0171 and D-0175 for evidence and receipt qualifications. Cite recorded foundations on each changed SPEC bullet under D-0122 and identify the ratified #313 plans as the extension. The merger records the completed existing-code execution policy extension and its relationships using decision tooling and rolls its citation into SPEC; the plumbing build cannot write decisions/. Unavailable Docker or network checks are Merger work, not a repair requirement by themselves. Provide the exact full integration command and require the merger to run it on the final head, post passing output and complete decision recording before moving to #294's next stage.

Kind: plumbing

usage.summary: Wrote `issues.json` with three sequential plumbing issues covering execution provenance, gate integration and receipts, then exhaustive and larger-bound checks. The plan passed its first check; `repo/` is unchanged.
